key_insight: AI detection of pulmonary tuberculosis on chest X-rays had pooled sensitivity of 89.6% and specificity of 68.9%, close to—but not clearly meeting—WHO triage targets of 90% and 70%.
clinical_relevance: AI-assisted chest X-ray interpretation may support TB screening and triage where radiologists are scarce, but performance varies by product and setting.
method: Systematic review of five databases covering January 2020–March 2026; 21 studies included.
Bivariate random-effects meta-analysis of nine evaluations from three independent clinical cohorts.
QUADAS-2 bias assessment, GRADE certainty assessment, and an overlap analysis using one evaluation per cohort.
evidence_signal: Sensitivity was 89.6% (95% CI 87.4–91.5%) and specificity 68.9% (64.2–73.2%); evidence certainty was low and very low, respectively.
watch_item: The review missed additional eligible evaluations, most assessed evaluations had high risk of bias, and broader deployment needs local threshold calibration and prospective external validation.
paper_title: Artificial intelligence for pulmonary tuberculosis detection on chest X-ray images: A systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis
